query: What does the upstream canary do, which decisions remain unresolved, and how is accepted source provenance checked?

context.answer:
Upstream canary: a separate read-only Kiro product/runtime canary, run weekly or by manual dispatch, outside the autonomous acceptance path (which covers only the GitHub source entries in maintenance/upstreams.json). It resolves the official stable Kiro CLI manifest, selects the x86_64 Linux headless archive, verifies and probes the advertised binary, validates and discovers the six workspace agents, and queries the live model inventory without sending a model turn. Checksum/version, six-agent validation, and model-inventory checks gate; IDE metadata, Kiro Crew Nightly feeds, changelog, llms.txt, and recorded doc hashes are bounded observations. It never edits a pin, candidate branch, workflow, or protected controller code; a newer stable CLI deliberately fails it until a human promotes each trust-root pin.

Accepted source provenance: the review-and-provenance sub-feature binds the ledger genesis and every accepted transition to canonical provenance markers, exhaustive A/B/C review evidence, semantic patch completeness, and an independent no-tool Kiro-hosted Claude Opus 5 review of the exact candidate. Parity accounts for every tracked source path (Cursor skill packages direct/alias/native-replacement/excluded; generic OKF sources exact A/B/C dispositions), and acceptance freshly revalidates proposal, parity, tests, and ownership before one atomic ledger append and pin advance. Packaged provenance documents stay in existing package locations.

Unresolved decisions: no source records an explicit open-question list; only scope limits (e.g. Web support untested) and statements that decisions do not prove implementation.
